material_gaps: The held own term (officers 'shall be returned to the Coast and Geodetic Survey when the present national emergency ceases to exist') is a trigger, and no held source fixes which emergency is meant or when it ceased (the 1941 emergency proclamation and the statute terminating wartime emergencies are not held).
No held record that the five officers were in fact returned, and no held CURRENT: predicate.
notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: BLOCKED, leaning NO. I read the complete order text within the held extract of EO 9007 (7 FR 95, Jan. 2, 1942; the extract also carries the tail of the Hawaii distressed-area order and the start of EO 9006 on State employment-security personnel): five named Coast and Geodetic Survey officers are transferred to the Navy Department under 33 U.S.C. 855 'in view of the existing national emergency', serve as part of the naval forces under Navy orders, and 'shall be returned to the Coast and Geodetic Survey when the present national emergency ceases to exist.' It is a closed-class wartime transfer with an express end trigger and no savings clause. The Hawaii 'distressed emergency area' TERM hit in the machine record belongs to the neighbouring order and is not used. The history is an empty catalog note. A NO by own term is very plausible (the wartime emergency long ended and the five officers are gone), but the trigger event is a fact needing a source: the held record does not identify the emergency by proclamation or fix when it ceased, so I would be supplying the ending date from memory, which the procedure forbids. I request the wartime emergency proclamation and the termination instrument (and any record of the officers' return).
